title: Combining Hilbert coefficients into a controlled common-power marking
statement:
Let $X\hookrightarrow Z$ be a reduced closed finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme in a smooth scheme, $a\in X$, and $H_0=H_X(a)$, with $H_X\le_{\rm lex}H_0$ on the neighbourhood considered [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant]. Work locally about $a$, allowing a further restriction of the supplied neighbourhood. Supply a regular Hilbert coefficient datum [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum]: a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$, regular coefficient functions $c_{i\gamma}$, vertex degrees $d_i$, and division-adapted Taylor generators satisfying its five homogeneous-division, generation and Jacobian conditions, with jet bound $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ (vacuous for an empty vertex list). Put $m_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|>0$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$. For any positive common multiple $b$ of these finitely many weights, define the actual ideal
$$I_b=\sum_{i,\,|\gamma|<d_i}(c_{i\gamma}^{\,b/m_{i\gamma}})\subset\mathcal O_N.$$
For an empty vertex list take $b=1$ and $I_b=0$. This ideal is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Its order cosupport [def-trf-marked-ideal-order] is exactly the coefficient order locus and, as a subset of $Z$, exactly $\{x\in X:H_X(x)=H_0\}$.
Let $C$ be a smooth closed center in that locus, having normal crossings with a supplied ordered coordinate-hyperplane boundary transverse to $N$; this means etale coordinates make $N,C$ coordinate subspaces and each boundary component a distinct coordinate hyperplane [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $\sigma:Z'\to Z$ be its blowup and let $X',N'$ be scheme-theoretic strict transforms [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. On every chart meeting $N'$ with exceptional equation $e$, the functions $c'_{i\gamma}=e^{-m_{i\gamma}}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$ are regular, and their combined ideal satisfies
$$\sum_{i,\gamma}((c'_{i\gamma})^{b/m_{i\gamma}})=e^{-b}\sigma^*I_b.$$
At every point $x'\in X'$ over $C$, $H_{X'}(x')\le_{\rm lex}H_0$; equality holds exactly on this transformed ideal's cosupport on $N'$. At equality points the transformed generators retain the same diagram and all five conditions of the supplied coefficient datum. Charts missing $N'$ have no equality points. Outside $C$, the schemes, ideal and Hilbert--Samuel values are identified with the original ones. More generally, for any smooth center in $X$ on which $H_X$ is locally constant, its ambient blowup satisfies $H_{X'}(x')\le_{\rm lex}H_X(\sigma(x'))$ at every point of the strict transform, using local coefficient data near the center.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; BM 1997 Theorems 7.20, 9.4, 9.6; BMT 6.2. Common-power construction and one-step transform from old proof steps 3,4. No Stacks tag states the Hilbert coefficient transform package.

proof.text: On the smooth coefficient scheme N, local finite type over the field gives local Noetherianity. Every quasi-coherent ideal is then of finite type. Convert this to finite type of its module by [lem-pqf-finite-type-ideal-module]. Its module is the kernel of O_N to the closed-subscheme pushforward of its structure sheaf; the closed-immersion pushforward theorem in [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] give quasi-coherence. Apply [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. This applies to the actual common-power ideal, also for an empty list. Smoothness and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] give regular local stalk rings for step 2.

At each stalk of N choose a minimal finite generating set of its maximal ideal. Its size is the dimension by regularity, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes it a regular sequence. By [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] the associated graded ring is a polynomial ring over the residue field, hence a domain. The product formula [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure] gives [c]^q=[c^q] in degree q times the degree of c. If c is not in m^d, choose its first nonzero initial form in degree r<d. For q>0 its qth power is nonzero, whereas c^q in m^(dq) would put it in m^(rq+1), a contradiction. Conversely, c in m^d implies c^q in m^(dq) by ideal multiplication. Thus c^(b/w) in m^b iff c in m^w when w divides b>0. Directly from the supremum definition of ideal order, b<=ord(I) iff I is contained in m^b: if containment fails, every admissible exponent is at most b-1. On affine N the stalk of ofIdealTop is the image of the global ideal under the germ map, by germ-restriction compatibility. Map the generating span and test containment on each displayed coefficient power; apply the preceding power equivalence and w*(b/w)=b. Empty lists give the zero ideal and vacuous inequalities.

source.place: Tags 00KU, 00NQ and 00LN; associated-graded initial-form argument implementing ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 common-power order calculation.

proof.text: Apply the existing coefficient_equality_germ declaration of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] to p,i,a, the ordered vertices, Q bound and supplied datum. It already compares the intrinsic normalized HilbertSamuel.function at every point, including nonclosed points, so no separate jet theorem is invoked. Retain its open neighbourhood V. Rewrite membership in the image of the coefficient order locus as an existential coefficient point and use the pointwise equivalence of step 2. For s=0 the generating span is empty and its ideal sheaf is zero, directly from the definition.

proof.text: For each low coefficient apply [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] on the same smooth flag to $J=(c_{i\gamma})$ with mark $m_{i\gamma}$. Its coherence follows as in step 1, and the center-order hypothesis is step 2. It gives $c_{i\gamma}\in\mathcal I_{C,N}^{m_{i\gamma}}$ and regular quotients $c\prime_{i\gamma}=e^{-m_{i\gamma}}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$ on the smooth $N\prime$. This node also gives the chart description, including components removed by the center. The same application to $(I_b,b)$ gives the regular coherent controlled ideal on every chart meeting $N\prime$.

proof.text: In a chart of step 4, integer exponentiation gives $(e^{-m}c)^{b/m}=e^{-b}c^{b/m}$, because $m(b/m)=b$. Pullback of a generated ideal is generated by the pulled-back generators, so summing this identity proves $\sum((c\prime_{i\gamma})^{b/m_{i\gamma}})=e^{-b}\sigma^*I_b$. Changing $e$ by a unit changes each generator by a unit power and preserves this ideal identity. Empty sums on both sides are zero.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94, historical resolution input. Agent assembly using the separately stated formal coefficient transform criterion; BM 1997 Theorems 7.20, 9.4, 9.6 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: At a point above $C$, use the blowup part of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] on the supplied datum at its image in $C$. Its five conditions hold there because $C$ lies in the coefficient locus; the center is coordinate by hypothesis. It proves $H_{X\prime}\le H_0$, equality exactly on $N\prime$ with the transformed coefficient inequalities, and persistence of all five conditions and the diagram at equality. [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] again identifies these extended jet functions with the stated $H$. Apply the product-order and sum-order assertions of [lem-trf-logarithmic-differential-transform] on the smooth $N\prime$ (the computation of step 2) to its regular coefficients from step 4: the inequalities are exactly cosupport of the ideal in step 5. The formal criterion excludes equality on all charts missing $N\prime$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94, historical resolution input. Agent assembly using the separately stated formal coefficient transform criterion; BM 1997 Theorems 7.20, 9.4, 9.6 (local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Over $Z\setminus C$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies the ambient schemes and [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] identifies both strict transforms with their original restrictions. The exceptional ideal is the unit ideal there, so the controlled ideal identifies with $I_b$. The local rings are isomorphic, hence their maximal-ideal quotients and residue-field transcendence degrees agree; thus $H$ agrees as well.

proof.text: For a general smooth locally $H$-constant center $C$, fix $x\in C$ and restrict so that $H_X=H_X(x)$ on $C$. [lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data] supplies data at $x$ for a sufficiently large $Q$ on an etale neighbourhood $U$ with $H\le H_X(x)$. The initial equality criterion of step 3 places this portion of $C$ in $N$ as a set; $C$ is smooth, hence reduced, so it factors through the closed $N$. Coordinates: [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ for $N\hookrightarrow U$ gives, on an open $U_1\ni x$, an etale $h:U_1\to\mathbf A^{a+r}$ with $N\cap U_1=V(h_{a+1},\ldots,h_{a+r})$, these pullbacks generating the ideal of $N$ and forming a regular sequence, and $N\cap U_1\to\mathbf A^a$ etale, so $N$ has dimension $a$ at $x$. The same lemma for $C\hookrightarrow N$ gives an open $N_0\ni x$ of $N$ and an etale $g:N_0\to\mathbf A^a$ with $C\cap N_0$ the vanishing locus of its last coordinates. Shrink $U_1$ to an affine open with $U_1\cap N\subseteq N_0$; the closed subscheme $U_1\cap N$ is affine, so the $g_j$ lift to $\tilde g_j\in\mathcal O(U_1)$. Then $h'=(\tilde g,h_{a+1},\ldots,h_{a+r})$ restricts to $g$ on $N$, and $h'^{-1}(\mathbf A^a\times0)=N\cap U_1$, so the square with the coordinate inclusion is cartesian. [lem-pur-etale-near-regular-coordinate-fibre] makes $h'$ etale near $x$: in these coordinates $N$ and $C$ are coordinate subspaces. Take empty boundary. Steps 4--6 give nonincrease above $x$; step 7 gives equality away from the center. This proves the pointwise comparison with the image, even when different components of the center have different constant values.
